court: Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit

issues.label: Article III standing—individual plaintiffs
issues.why: Court must determine whether plaintiffs who now receive benefits have injury-in-fact and redressability.

issues.label: Standing—Empower Missouri diversion of resources
issues.why: Court must decide if the organization's expenditures constitute a cognizable injury under Havens/FDA v. AAM.

issues.label: Mootness of individual claims
issues.why: All individual plaintiffs now receive SNAP benefits, raising whether their claims are moot.

issues.label: Capable-of-repetition-yet-evading-review exception
issues.why: Court must assess if this exception preserves otherwise moot claims given ongoing recertification risk.

issues.label: Voluntary cessation doctrine
issues.why: Approvals came after suit was filed, implicating whether defendant's conduct moots claims.

issues.label: Redressability of requested injunctive relief
issues.why: Court must ensure ordered relief would remedy plaintiffs' claimed injuries.

issues.label: Private right of action under SNAP Act
issues.why: Court must decide whether §§2014(a) and 2020(e)(2)(B) create privately enforceable rights.

issues.label: Enforceability via 42 U.S.C. §1983
issues.why: Whether SNAP provisions confer individual rights enforceable through section 1983.

issues.label: First-day-filing right under §2020(e)(2)(B)
issues.why: Court must interpret whether the statute guarantees same-day application opportunity.

issues.label: Interview timing and 30-day denial policy
issues.why: Whether automatic denial for failure to interview violates SNAP requirements.

issues.label: Protected property interest in SNAP benefits
issues.why: Due process claim requires establishing a constitutionally protected entitlement.

issues.label: Procedural due process adequacy
issues.why: Court must determine what process is due and whether DSS's practices satisfied it.

issues.label: Mathews v. Eldridge balancing
issues.why: Due process analysis requires weighing private interest, error risk, and government burden.

issues.label: Distinction between denial and access failure
issues.why: Whether phone/scheduling barriers constitute a deprivation versus mere administrative delay.

issues.label: ADA Title II coverage of SNAP administration
issues.why: Court must confirm DSS services fall within Title II's public-services provisions.

issues.label: Meaningful access / reasonable accommodation standard
issues.why: Whether DSS denied disabled plaintiffs meaningful access requiring accommodation.

issues.label: Qualified individual with a disability
issues.why: Court must find Dallas and Holmes are disabled and qualified under the ADA.

issues.label: Notice/request of accommodation requirement
issues.why: Whether DSS had knowledge triggering a duty to accommodate.

issues.label: Section 504 Rehabilitation Act claim basis
issues.why: Relief references Section 504 though claims focus on ADA, requiring analysis of its applicability.

issues.label: ADA grievance procedures obligation
issues.why: Whether failure to adopt grievance procedures independently violates the ADA.

issues.label: Standing for Holmes's ADA claim
issues.why: Holmes's disability basis for ADA relief must be established individually.

issues.label: Eleventh Amendment sovereign immunity
issues.why: Official-capacity suit against state official implicates immunity and Ex parte Young exception.

issues.label: ADA abrogation of state immunity
issues.why: Court must determine whether Title II validly abrogates immunity for these claims.

issues.label: Standard for permanent injunctive relief
issues.why: Court must apply eBay factors including irreparable harm and inadequate legal remedy.

issues.label: Scope and specificity of injunction
issues.why: Whether 26 operational requirements and numeric benchmarks exceed proper equitable tailoring.

issues.label: Numeric wait-time and denial-rate mandates
issues.why: Whether court-imposed 20-minute/20% quotas are supported by law and record.

issues.label: Federalism and institutional-reform concerns
issues.why: Ordering statewide policy overhaul raises comity and separation-of-powers limits.

issues.label: Reporting to legislative/executive branches
issues.why: Requiring reports to other government branches may exceed judicial authority.

issues.label: PLRA/Prison-style needs-narrowness limits
issues.why: Court should ensure injunction is narrowly drawn to violations, though PLRA may not apply.

issues.label: Federal waiver of interview requirement
issues.why: Bax's asserted recertification waiver, absent from record, affects merits and remedy.

issues.label: Standard of review on summary judgment
issues.why: Court must apply de novo review confirming no genuine disputes of material fact.

issues.label: Substitution of defendant Bax for Knodell
issues.why: Official-capacity substitution under Rule 25(d) must be properly recognized.

issues.label: Empower Missouri organizational standing scope
issues.why: Whether organization can pursue relief beyond its own diverted-resource injury.
